basics.name: Ha Nguyen
basics.label: Hardware & Network Systems Architect (Ph.D.)
basics.summary: Innovative Hardware Systems Architect & Senior Network Systems Architect with 3+ years of postdoctoral R&D and 5+ years of university research leadership. Proven expert in translating advanced transport protocols, Software-Defined Networking (SDN) control planes, and P4 data planes into high-performance physical silicon and RTL datapaths (SystemVerilog/Verilog) across Intel Agilex/Stratix and AMD Xilinx Kintex UltraScale+ architectures.

work.name: University of Science
work.summary: Directed R&D initiatives within ICTLAB focusing on loss-masking transport frameworks, P4 data-plane telemetry, active queue management (AQM), adaptive SDN routing, and wireless sensor networks.
highlights: Supervised 20+ researchers and secured over $100k in R&D funding.
Architected P4 telemetry tracking and dynamic SDN control frameworks.

work.name: Kyushu Institute of Technology
work.summary: Served as Principal Investigator (PI) for two JSPS KAKEN Grants-in-Aid (4.42M JPY).
highlights: Engineered resilient TCP/NC transport frameworks and dynamic SDN routing control planes.
Masked channel losses and prevented TCP timeout degradation under high BER conditions.

work.name: University of Science
work.summary: Taught telecommunication & computer networking courses while managing departmental L2/L3 infrastructure.
highlights: Architected an FPGA-based 2x2 MIMO-OFDM SDM Transceiver (400 Mbps) using custom DSP pipelines.
Mentored student teams to 2nd place in Cisco NetRiders national competition.
Dissertation: Studies on Improvement and Application of TCP with Network Coding in Lossy Networks.

awards.title: International Conference Best Paper Awards (3-Time Recipient)
awards.summary: Recipient of 3 international conference Best Paper Awards (2019, 2020, 2022) for protocol and wireless emulation research.

awards.title: JSPS KAKEN Grants-in-Aid Principal Investigator
awards.awarder: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
awards.summary: Awarded 2 competitive research grants (Grant IDs 18H06467 & 20K19785) totaling 4.42 Million JPY for self-healing network protocols.

awards.title: Cisco Instructor Years of Service & Student Competition Award
awards.summary: Cisco Certified Academy Instructor (CCAI); mentored student team to 2nd place in the Cisco NetRiders National Competition.

certificates.name: CCAI (Cisco Certified Academy Instructor) - CCNA & Security

skills.name: Hardware & Digital Logic Design (RTL)
keywords: FPGA (Intel Agilex/Stratix, AMD Xilinx Kintex UltraScale+)

projects.name: High-Speed Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL) Link Emulation
projects.summary: Architected a multi-vendor HITL emulation system bridging Intel Agilex 5 and Xilinx Kintex UltraScale+ FPGAs over HSMC-XTS and PCIe 3.0x4 interfaces.
highlights: Designed an ultra-wide 1024-bit datapath operating at 156.25/312.5 MHz (up to 320 Gbps pipeline capacity).

projects.name: Real-Time AWGN Hardware Generator
projects.summary: Designed 512-bit wide AXI-Stream datapaths achieving 375MHz+ on Intel Agilex 7 and Xilinx FPGAs.
highlights: Implemented APB interfaces for dynamic C/C++ SDN software control.
Automated TCL synthesis and build flows.

projects.name: Programmable Data Plane (P4) for Telemetry & Loss Mitigation
projects.summary: Architected a hop-by-hop multicast packet loss recovery scheme using P4 BMv2 switches and ns-3.
highlights: Designed a custom 8-byte Control Header with a 40-bit sequence for microsecond-precision in-band telemetry tracking.
